stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave.
stories.excerpt: GFP Real Estate announced that Zimmet Law Group P.C. has signed a new office lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Ave. in Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet Law Group will occupy Suite 603 on the sixth floor of the building under a new 10-year lease, relocating its Manhattan office from 477 Madison Ave. The firm is expected to take occupancy following completion of its new space later this year. Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone of GFP Real Estate represented the landlord in-house. Elliot Zelinger of Savitt Partners represented Zimmet Law Group. “Zimmet Law Group’s decision to make a long-term commitment to 515 Madison Avenue speaks to the continued appeal of the building and the strength of the Plaza District,” said McGrath. “Professional services firms continue to prioritize high-quality, well-located office space, and we’re pleased to welcome Zimmet Law Group to the building.” The post Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave. appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Zimmet Law Group leases 5,476 sq ft at 515 Madison Ave, Manhattan Plaza District.
10-year commitment signals professional services demand in high-quality Manhattan office space.
Firm relocates from 477 Madison Ave, indicating tenant retention in premium Plaza District.
stories.summary: Zimmet Law Group P.C. signed a 10-year lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's Plaza District, relocating from nearby 477 Madison Ave. The deal reflects continued appetite among professional services firms for long-term, well-located office space. Landlord representatives highlighted the transaction as evidence of sustained Plaza District appeal.
stories.impact: Minor relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing strength in Manhattan Plaza District does not directly affect apartment demand, supply, or feasibility, though robust white-collar employment and professional services concentration in this submarket supports nearby residential renter bases.

stories.title: Avison Young Recapitalization Provides “War Chest” for Further Growth
stories.excerpt: Avison Young’s newly announced recapitalization does more than deleverage the company’s balance sheet debt-to-EBITDA ratio to less than 3x, reduce debt and preferred equity by nearly 70% and give key financial partners a common equity position, although it accomplishes all of these. “We’re pretty excited,” Avison Young chair and CEO Mark E. Rose told Connect CRE. “This gives us the war chest to do the things that we’re known for”–namely, make strategic acquisitions, broaden the platform’s capabilities and expand the pool of talent through recruitment. “And we have our eyes on targets.” Expected to close in October, the new transaction builds upon the success of the company’s 2024 recapitalization. It also represents a rethinking of how to produce the best outcome for Avison Young’s longtime financial stakeholders as well as the company’s principals.   “It’s kind of simple,” said Rose. “Was it better to take the money and pay these [stakeholders], or was it better to invest and make them multiples of the same money? And after 16 months, that’s what we were able to come to.”  The process of devising this solution began in the spring of 2025, Rose said. The company looked at various options for taking the stakeholders’ investment and “putting it into a different form that would meet everybody’s needs.”  The solution entailed a 70% debt-to-equity swap, “giving us a debt-to-EBITDA ratio that’s under 3x so that we can build, effectively, a fund—a pool of capital along with additional new money that [the stakeholders] were putting in,” said Rose.  He continued, “What we needed to do was work with our financial stakeholders, convert them into equity holders.” Their ownership stake is
bullets: Avison Young recapitalization reduces debt-to-EBITDA below 3x, cuts debt 70%, closing October.
Company gains 'war chest' for strategic acquisitions and talent expansion across platform.
Move signals CRE services sector consolidation and M&A acceleration in multifamily brokerage.
stories.summary: Avison Young completed a recapitalization that reduces debt-to-EBITDA to below 3x and cuts debt and preferred equity by nearly 70%, expected to close in October. The transaction gives the firm capital for strategic acquisitions, capability expansion, and talent recruitment. CEO Mark Rose framed the move as converting shareholder returns into multiples through reinvestment rather than immediate payouts.
stories.impact: Signals increased M&A and consolidation activity in CRE services. Better-capitalized brokerage platforms accelerate acquisitions of smaller brokerages and teams, increasing competition for deals and data in multifamily markets—expect tighter bid processes and faster market intelligence among major brokers underwriting development sites.

stories.title: Local Owner-Operator Snags Pico-Robertson Apartment Property
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1476 S Shenandoah St., a 16-unit multifamily property in Los Angeles. The property sold for $5.3 million, or $334,937 per unit. “Properties like this rarely become available in Pico-Robertson, especially those that have been held by the same ownership for more than two decades,” said Sam Liberow, senior managing director investments. “After 23 years of ownership, the offering generated six competitive offers, reflecting continued demand for well-located multifamily assets with large floor plans. The buyer plans to renovate units through natural tenant turnover while holding the property as a long-term investment.” Liberow, in Marcus & Millichap’s Encino office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, 1476 Shenandoah Street LLC. He also procured the buyer, a local owner and operator. Built in 1966, the 17,653-square-foot property is situated on a 0.30-acre parcel in Los Angeles’ Pico-Robertson neighborhood. The post Local Owner-Operator Snags Pico-Robertson Apartment Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap closed sale of 16-unit Pico-Robertson property for $5.3M ($334,937/unit).
Property held 23 years generated six competitive offers; buyer plans hold-and-renovate strategy.
Large floor plans and scarcity of offerings in submarket drove competitive bid environment.
stories.summary: A 16-unit multifamily property at 1476 S Shenandoah Street in Los Angeles's Pico-Robertson neighborhood sold for $5.3 million ($334,937 per unit) to a local owner-operator. Built in 1966 on 0.30 acres, the property generated six competitive bids after 23 years of single ownership. The buyer plans long-term ownership with unit renovations through natural turnover.
stories.impact: Pico-Robertson's scarcity of well-located small multifamily assets driving cap-rate compression and owner-operator competition in Los Angeles. Limited supply of underutilized legacy buildings with large floor plans in established neighborhoods signals opportunity for development sites or value-add conversions—demand for product exceeds available inventory, supporting rents and reducing development risk for similar-profile new construction.

stories.title: Grocery-Anchored Queens Retail Secures $32M Financing
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s New York Metro Debt + Equity team, led by Robert Delitsky and Charles Cotsalas, arranged $32 million in financing for Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot retail property located in the Springfield Gardens neighborhood of Queens. Delitsky and Cotsalas arranged financing on behalf of the owner, Mattone Group Springnex LLC, through Principal Financial Group. “Ownership developed Springnex Plaza in 2000 and they have done a fabulous job maintaining very strong occupancy,” Delitsky said. “Supermarket-anchored shopping centers like Springnex Plaza will continue to attract very strong lender interest in today’s market,” added Cotsalas. Springnex Plaza is a 100% occupied, multi-tenant, grocery-anchored retail center situated on approximately 5.58 acres. Serving the Springfield Gardens community for more than two decades, Springnex Plaza offers a complementary mix of grocery, dining, healthcare and service-oriented tenants. Anchored by Stop & Shop, It is home to a diverse roster of local and national retailers, including Ashley Stewart, IHOP Restaurant, and Northwell Health. The post Grocery-Anchored Queens Retail Secures $32M Financing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranged $32M financing for Springnex Plaza grocery-anchored retail in Queens Springfield Gardens.
100% occupied 96,028 sq ft center anchored by Stop & Shop; lender confidence high.
Supermarket-anchored centers attracting strong institutional capital in today's market environment.
stories.summary: Northmarq's New York Metro team arranged $32 million in financing for Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot grocery-anchored retail center in Springfield Gardens, Queens, through Principal Financial Group. The property is 100% occupied and anchored by Stop & Shop with complementary grocery, dining, healthcare and service tenants. The deal reflects strong lender appetite for well-maintained, essential-use retail assets.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Grocery-anchored retail financing strength indicates healthy neighborhood foot traffic and tenant resilience in outer-borough Queens, which can support residential development rents in adjacent areas, but capital availability is concentrated in retail, not apartments.

stories.title: Brixton Capital Launches Multifamily Investment-Management Platform
stories.excerpt: Brixton Capital’s Residential division has launched an integrated multifamily investment-management initiative designed to help institutional investors, family offices, lenders, joint venture partners and other owners improve the performance and value of complex multifamily assets. The initiative combines Brixton’s institutional investment and asset management capabilities with the operating expertise of its affiliate, United Apartment Group. “We see a meaningful opportunity to partner with owners and investment groups that have good real estate but need a different investment-management solution,” said Brixton VP of residential acquisitions Mark Mandala. “There are many multifamily assets where the underlying property remains fundamentally attractive, but the existing sponsor may not have the capital, operating infrastructure or institutional asset-management capabilities required for the next phase of ownership. We believe this is a particularly compelling opportunity because we are not simply offering another property management solution—we can bring together the investment strategy and the execution platform under one roof.” Brixton’s Residential division is particularly focused on multifamily assets where ownership is seeking a new investment-management or operating partner, or where the property requires a broader restructuring of its business plan. The post Brixton Capital Launches Multifamily Investment-Management Platform appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Brixton Capital launches integrated multifamily investment-management platform combining acquisition and asset management.
Targets sponsor changes and asset restructuring opportunities; partners with affiliate United Apartment Group.
Platform aims to address capital, infrastructure, and operating gaps in complex multifamily assets.
stories.summary: Brixton Capital's Residential division launched an integrated investment-management platform designed to help institutional investors, family offices, lenders, and owners improve performance and value of complex multifamily assets. The initiative combines Brixton's institutional investment and asset management with the operating expertise of affiliate United Apartment Group. It targets assets where underlying property fundamentals are sound but sponsorship or capital structure requires overhaul.
stories.impact: Signals flight-to-quality and sponsor consolidation in multifamily. Brixton's focus on sponsor transitions and asset restructuring indicates a wave of underperforming or undercapitalized multifamily properties cycling to stronger operators. Developers facing debt maturity or capital calls should expect increased acquisition competition from well-funded platforms; opportune moment to sell stabilized assets or refinance before sponsor replacement becomes forced.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar completes $800M cash acquisition of Zonda, new-home construction data and developer platform.
Zonda serves 3,000+ homebuilders; generated ~$170M revenue in 2025; taps $400B new-home market.
CoStar gains lot-level construction and development data; signals data-driven real estate consolidation.
stories.summary: CoStar Group closed its $800 million cash acquisition of Zonda, a new-home construction data and homebuilder software platform. Zonda serves over 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers with proprietary lot-level construction and development intelligence, generating approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. The deal gives CoStar a direct foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market.
stories.impact: CoStar's acquisition consolidates market intelligence and data advantage in land and new-home development. Multifamily developers lose granular lot-level and competing-project visibility to a single dominant data provider; expect pricing pressure on data subscriptions and faster market saturation signals. For site selection and competitive positioning in core markets, developers should lock in long-term data partnerships or invest in proprietary land-pipeline intelligence before CoStar/Zonda integrate and raise barriers to entry.

stories.title: Michael Troyanovsky of Regency Development Group: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: With a population of less than 6,000, little Bay Harbor Islands, Fla., is often overlooked – but not by Regency Development Group. Since 2020, the developer has been building residential projects in the coastal community near Surfside, Indian Creek and Bal Harbour. Regency has four active projects on the island, including the 33-unit La Maré Regency, the nine-unit La Maré Signature and the 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Commercial Observer recently caught up with Michael Troyanovsky, managing partner and vice president of the family company, to discuss the submarket’s success. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity.   Commercial Observer: Why Bay Harbor Islands? What caught your interest about that submarket? Michael Troyanovsky: A really valid question, because there were other hot spot areas that a lot of people were gravitating to when we first started buying Bay Harbor. We came to the area, and we really felt like it had the most potential. It was always overlooked. It’s honestly the most amazing hidden gem. It’s surrounded by the most beautiful waters, a little nook in the center of Miami. It’s getting more and more discovered. Since then, we really integrated into the island, and we really got to know the local community, the local governments, because we have to work very closely with them on getting all the projects approved and making sure that it fits the neighborhood and demographic. We opened up a big sales office here, and we plan to stay here for the future. Who are you finding is the target demographic for your units? It’s a little bit of a mix demographic-wise, but I would say a lot of people who, whether it’s local or international, really want boutique building living. I’ve had the pleasure of meeting with all the people who purchased in the building and so many customers over the last few years, and all of them have said pretty much the same thing. bullets: Regency Development Group building four active projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida (pop. <6K).
Projects include 33-unit La Maré Regency, 9-unit La Maré Signature, 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas.

stories.summary: Regency Development Group has been actively building residential projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida, a coastal community of fewer than 6,000 residents near Surfside and Bal Harbour, since 2020. The developer currently operates four active projects, including a 33-unit and a 9-unit luxury property under the La Maré brand and a 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Managing partner Michael Troyanovsky cited the submarket's overlooked status and proximity to premium coastal amenities as driving appeal.
stories.impact: Signals luxury multifamily density migration in South Florida. Developer focus on small-scale, high-end residential in overlooked but affluent micro-submarkets near established luxury hubs (Bal Harbour, Surfside) indicates value-add opportunity via density and brand lift. Bay Harbor Islands' limited supply and constrained buildable land support premium rents; developers should monitor exclusionary zoning and local approval timelines as tighter approval processes may create barriers to entry and protect existing operators.

stories.title: JBL Asset Management Buys Retail Condo Near Miami Design District
stories.excerpt: Alta Developers sold off a retail condo near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million, property records show. JBL Asset Management purchased the 25,504-square-foot asset on the ground floor of the Quadro condo building. The property at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard faces train tracks, just east of the Miami Design District, an open-air, luxury mall. Quadro’s retail tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture store and Waterworks plumbing supply store. Hollywood, Fla.-based JBL is marketing a 2,358-square-foot suite as the last remaining retail space at the 407,498-square-foot condo building. Alta Developers completed the 200-unit building in 2019. The purchase comes as the 18-block Design District, one of the country’s highest-grossing upscale malls, is undergoing a major expansion. Earlier this week, its owners, entities tied to Miami-based Craig Robins and LVMH billionaire Bernard Arnault, scored a $125 million construction loan to build a Snøhetta-designed, mixed-use building. The joint venture also launched sales for Fouquet’s condo and hotel development, designed by Pritzker Prize winner David Chipperfield. Representatives for Alta Developers and JBL Asset Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: JBL Asset Management acquires retail condo near Miami Design District for $17.3M.
25,504 sq ft ground-floor retail at Quadro building; Design District expanding $125M mixed-use.
Retail condo sale adjacent to luxury district expansion signals capital deployment near mixed-use anchor.
stories.summary: JBL Asset Management purchased a 25,504-square-foot ground-floor retail condo at the Quadro building near Miami's Design District for $17.3 million. The property is anchored by tenants including The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture, and Waterworks. The purchase occurs as the Design District—a high-grossing luxury mall—begins a $125 million mixed-use expansion financed through a joint venture involving Craig Robins and LVMH's Bernard Arnault.
stories.impact: Miami Design District's mixed-use and hospitality expansion (Fouquet's condo/hotel by Chipperfield) signals strong residential demand and foot traffic near the anchor. Ground-floor retail acquisition and construction loans indicate capital confidence in supporting mixed-use density; developers should evaluate residential components in nearby corridors along Biscayne Boulevard—proximity to luxury retail and hospitality drives renter demographics and command premium rents.

stories.title: Now Is the Time to Buy in Commercial Real Estate: Morgan Stanley
stories.excerpt: Despite a bumpy economy and increasingly high Treasury yields, one global investment firm believes now is the time to pounce on U.S. commercial real estate. Commercial Observer spoke with Tony Charles, global head of research and strategy at Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, who outlined the main takeaways from Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s mid-year 2026 real estate outlook. After a four-year recession, commercial real estate is now being repriced, giving investors a chance to acquire prime assets at low prices; supply is down across the board; and megatrends in AI, global supply chains, and aging demographics have opened up attractive entry points into infrastructure, retail and senior housing. “We certainly believe we’re entering the next up-cycle for real estate. It’s an attractive entry point,” Charles told CO in a Thursday interview. “And, given the repricing that’s now below replacement costs, we’re pretty confident in the next vintage of real estate investing.” Charles argued that the recent U.S. real estate downturn — which began in mid-2022 amid the Federal Reserve’s policy U-turn to hike interest rates coming out of COVID-19 — created “the longest downturn for real estate since the 1980s and early 1990s,” and that four years later, pricing is still down an average of 20 percent across the board. But he noted that “supply is down dramatically, so that’s obviously very helpful for real estate,” and that a strong structural macroeconomic backdrop — U.S. GDP grew 2.1 percent year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026 — has provided “a lot of green shoots that are beginning to show through.” He pointed out that CRE transaction activity increased 23 percent year-over-year in the U.S., institutional capital raising is up nearly 40 percent on the year, and that CRE debt originations are up around 20 percent year-over-year. bullets: Morgan Stanley: U.S. commercial real estate repriced below replacement cost; entering next up-cycle.
Supply down across board; AI, supply-chain, aging-demographics megatrends open infrastructure, retail, senior housing.
Firm cites attractive entry point after four-year CRE downturn and Fed policy normalization.
stories.summary: Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing outlined its mid-year 2026 outlook, arguing the U.S. is entering the next commercial real estate up-cycle with assets repriced below replacement cost. Tony Charles, global head of research at MSRIM, highlighted reduced supply across all asset classes and identified megatrends in AI, supply-chain reconfiguration, and aging demographics as creating attractive entry points in infrastructure, retail, and senior housing after a four-year downturn beginning in mid-2022.
stories.impact: Signals institutional capital readiness for multifamily acquisitions and new development. Below-replacement-cost repricing reduces hurdle rates and improves underwriting for new supply; however, senior housing emphasis indicates capital concentration in higher-barrier aging-demographic plays. Multifamily developers in secondary/tertiary markets should expect increased competition from institutional capital; advantage tilts to operators with existing land pipelines, entitlements, and operational scale to deploy capital faster than new entrants.

stories.title: Whole Foods to Open Daily Shop at Murray Hill’s 509 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: Whole Foods Market has leased a 9,000-square-foot retail space in Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood. The 15-year deal occupies a ground-floor space and outdoor terraces at 509 Third Avenue, according to a memorandum of lease filed in city records Friday morning. The 35-story, 229-unit apartment tower, known as the Murray, was developed by Kahen Properties with Lalezarian Properties. A spokesperson for Whole Foods confirmed the lease in an email to Commercial Observer, but declined to share further details. Whole Foods’ newest Manhattan location will be on the smaller side. The store will follow the Amazon-owned grocer’s new Whole Foods Market Daily Shop format. The quick-trip urban shops sell grab-and-go meals alongside fresh produce, meat, bakery items and local specialty foods, according to the company’s website. The format was first rolled out in nearby Lenox Hill in 2024, and has since arrived in cities nationwide. Additional locations in Brooklyn and Hoboken, N.J., were announced late last year. Most recently, the grocer signed a lease for 8,121 square feet to open a daily shop at 1524 Second Avenue on the Upper East Side. Kahen Properties’ Majid Kahen signed the lease memorandum for the landlord, while Paul Hilliard, vice president of real estate at Whole Foods, signed for the grocer. It is unclear whether either party worked with an outside brokerage. The asking rent for the ground-floor space was not disclosed in the memorandum, but retail space in the nearby Herald Square area was $394 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. Spokespeople for Kahen and Lalezarian Properties did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Whole Foods Market leases 9,000 sq ft at 509 Third Avenue, Murray Hill, Manhattan.
15-year deal for ground floor + terraces; Whole Foods Daily Shop format (quick-trip urban).
Store supports 229-unit Murray apartment tower; Daily Shop model expanded from Lenox Hill 2024.
stories.summary: Whole Foods Market leased 9,000 square feet at 509 Third Avenue in Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood for 15 years. The ground-floor space with outdoor terraces is in the Murray, a 229-unit apartment tower developed by Kahen Properties and Lalezarian Properties. Whole Foods will operate in its newer Daily Shop format—a quick-trip, grab-and-go model—first launched in nearby Lenox Hill in 2024 and now expanding to Brooklyn, Hoboken, and other cities.
stories.impact: Whole Foods Daily Shop proliferation strengthens neighborhood retail and pedestrian activation in Murray Hill and surrounding Manhattan East Side submarkets. Grocery tenant lock-in at a stabilized 229-unit building signals cross-asset validation: grocery anchors drive residential rent growth and resident retention. Developers underwriting residential near mass transit in Manhattan should prioritize ground-floor retail, especially fresh grocery and quick-service; Daily Shop model aligns with smaller urban footprints and higher sales per square foot, signaling rent-growth potential for nearby apartments.
